title: Accelerated bainite phase transformation under high magnetic field: A novel perspective on the enhanced mechanical properties of steel
abstract: The present study proposes the utilization of a high magnetic field to facilitate the bainite phase transformation, thereby optimizing the mechanical properties of steels. Findings reveal that the application of high magnetic fields (6 T and 12 T) during the bainite isothermal transformation process at 350 °C markedly promotes the formation of the bainite phase, increasing its volume fraction from 41.3% in the absence of a magnetic field to 59.4% and 84.2%, respectively. This enhancement leading to a substantial enhancement in the mechanical performance of bainitic steels. This effect is rooted in the modified thermodynamics of the bainitic transformation, where the magnetic field reduces the magnetic Gibbs free energy of bainite by 20.39 J/mol at 6 T and 106.47 J/mol at 12 T, thereby increases the driving force for phase transformation and lowers the nucleation barrier. Furthermore, the high magnetic field modulates the kinetics of the bainitic transformation through magnetostrictive effects and the regulation of alloying element diffusion rates, promoting NbC precipitation and significantly elevating the geometrically necessary dislocation density (GND). These microstructural changes facilitate grain refinement and provide abundant nucleation sites for bainite. Consequently, this work introduces a novel and efficient strategy for the rapid development of high-performance bainitic steels.
